newsitem.title: USA: Stocks mixed, bonds firm before data; dollar weaker.
newsitem.headline: Stocks mixed, bonds firm before data; dollar weaker.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell Monday, ending a string of six record closing highs, but the broader market continued its rally to new highs.
Bonds rose for the third straight session ahead of a slew of economic reports due Tuesday.
The dollar fell on fears about Japanese trade surpluses and as European Union leaders ended a two-week dispute on stabilising budgets for currency union.

The Dow Jones industrials average ended down 9.95 points at 7,772.09, slipping below Friday's record finish of 7,782.04. Declining issues led advances 1,239 to 1,227 on volume of 414 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The index of 30-blue chip stocks had jumped 477 points, or 6.5 percent as Wall Street celebrated good news that the economy was not overheating and inflation was still in check.
"Even God rested on the seventh day," said Charles White, managing director at Avatar Associates.
But whatever profit taking there was in blue chips did not spread to the broader market.
The strongest of the major indexes was the Nasdaq composite index, which rose 8.92 points to 1,431.95, its second record closing in a row.
The Standard & Poor's 500 index managed a gain of 0.63 of a point to 893.90, its seventh consecutive record finish.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 8,419.854, up 9.929, or 0.12 percent.
Buying in high-technology stocks, which had lagged the recent rally in blue chips, lifted the Nasdaq market.
"You're seeing a rally in the big-cap high tech names," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co.

In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury rose 13/32, or $4.0625 on a $1,000 bond, sending its yield down to 6.69 percent from 6.73 percent at Friday's close. The price and the yield move in opposite directions.
The dollar fell to 113.43 Japanese yen and 1.7315 German marks from 114.80 yen and 1.7353 marks late Friday.

Soybean prices fell sharply, weakened by nearly ideal growing weather for newly planted crops in the United States and renewed concern about the prospects of imports from South America. At the Chicago Board of Trade, soybeans for July delivery closed 16 cents a bushel lower at $8.38-1/2.
Wheat for July delivery on the CBOT closed 9-3/4 cents a bushel lower at $3.42-3/4.

At the New York Mercantile Exchange, crude oil prices remained rangebound in quiet trade as players awaited fresh news on the renewal of Iraqi oil sales under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, traders said.
Crude oil for delivery in July ended 18 cents higher at $19.01 a barrel after a day of lackluster trading that saw it trade up to $19.18 and down to $18.77.
Gasoline for delivery in July settled 0.63 cent higher at 58.03 cents a gallon, while heating oil for July delivery rose 0.30 cent settling at 51.94 cents a gallon.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 closed at 4,745.1, down 38.0 points, or 0.79 percent. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,681.07, up 152.72 points, or 0.74 percent.
